newsitem.title: USA: Montgomery Ward reports loss for second quarter.
newsitem.headline: Montgomery Ward reports loss for second quarter.

text.p: Montgomery Ward Holding Co. posted a loss of $216 million for the second quarter compared with a profit last year after customers strayed to competitors and sales fell despite markdowns.

Montgomery Ward reported results in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission for the period that ended June 28, which was just days before it filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in Delaware.
Last year the company earned $22 million during the second quarter.

Chicago-based Montgomery Ward said revenues fell 11 percent to $1.4 billion. Sales at the company's stores dropped 15 percent to $1.2 billion, and revenues at its insurance business and direct marketing division, including the Signature Group, rose 19 percent to $214 million.
At Montgomery Ward department stores "all product categories experienced sales decreases ranging from 12 percent to 20 percent," the company said.
"The company believes the decline in net sales in the second quarter 1997 reflected a decline in market share compared to competitors," it said.
To clear its shelves of a mountain of unsold goods, Montgomery Wardrices on electronics, housewares and apparel, damaging margins during the period.

In addition, spending rose on advertising, and expenses for assets writedowns and severance payments contributed to the loss, the company said. Montgomery Ward eliminated 400 jobs at its corporate headquarters and closed three of its stores earlier this year.
Thursday a bankruptcy judge approved Montgomery Ward's request to liquidate the merchandise, fixtures and leases of 33 Lechmere consumer electronics stores.
Schottenstein Bernstein Capital Group will conduct the liquidation, which was expected to produce proceeds of between $150 million and $160 million for Montgomery Ward.
The retailer was expected to close more stores to shore up losses, although it has not disclosed how many.

In its filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, Montgomery Ward said it would improve its financial performance by "slowing expansion, controlling expenses, closing certain unprofitable stores and completing its inventory reduction program."
